material_changes.title: Discovery Certification Protocol proposes executable audits for AI-research-agent novelty claims
verified_facts: arXiv:2609.09219 is titled 'Scores Alone Do Not Prove Discovery: The Discovery Certification Protocol for Auditing AI Research Agents' and is categorized under Multiagent Systems, Artificial Intelligence, and Software Engineering rather than cs.CR.

The paper proposes sealed evaluation, matched-agent recovery tests, recovery witnesses, finite-sample recovery bounds, optional truthful-feedback effect tests, and a deterministic LLM-free verifier over frozen evidence.

The authors report two controlled audits with zero recoveries in 96 episodes each and an upper recovery bound of 0.0468, plus paired feedback studies with 30 truthful recoveries and zero neutral recoveries; these are author-reported experimental results, not independently reproduced repository guarantees.

PyPI currently exposes dcp-audit 0.4.2 as an Apache-2.0 Python 3.11+ package and reports Trusted Publishing provenance tied to the cxcscmu/Discovery-Certification-Protocol repository at commit 59ca3a95fe8bf87e408b5940330e99e002675293.
The provenance-linked GitHub source repository is reported as private by PyPI, so repository-source inspection is not currently available from the public GitHub surface.
missing_verification: Independently install dcp-audit and dcp-harness in an isolated environment and reproduce their deterministic verifier/harness behavior on benign local fixtures.
Inspect package source distributions and dependency metadata before adopting code, because the provenance-linked GitHub repository is private.
Compare DCP's sealed-evaluation, recovery-witness, null-control, and evidence-bundle model against this repository's current research/intelligence provenance and independent-verification contracts.
Do not claim that DCP proves novelty or discovery outside its declared audit assumptions; preserve negative/ambiguous reproduction results if encountered.

If its deterministic bundle verifier is reproducible and materially improves the suite's evidence model, propose a separate integration item rather than importing it directly from this research pass.
